## P3 - Robot release-check suite runs a nonexistent `capture` command

**Location:** [tests/14-clabernetes/02-release-check.robot:26-38](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/tests/14-clabernetes/02-release-check.robot#L26-L38)

**Problem:** The FOR loop in the &#34;Cluster commands fail before the first cluster call&#34; test includes `capture -t ${topo} --list` and asserts stderr contains `no spec.runState` and the required-release string. No `capture` subcommand is registered in this tree&#58; `subcommandRegisterFuncs()` in [`cmd/root.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/cmd/root.go#L1-L1) lists 17 commands and no `Use:` literal anywhere in `cmd/` is `capture`, so cobra fails with an unknown-command error whose stderr contains neither expected string.

**Trigger:** Running the suite with `CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG` set &#40;it is skipped by default&#41;.

**Impact:** The release-gating suite — the exact scenario this PR&#39;s support check is built for — fails at the `capture` item regardless of the old cluster&#39;s state, and the follow-up assertion that `deploy` created no namespace &#40;lines 40-43&#41; is never reached for that item. Merged in isolation, the PR cannot pass its own test suite; this likely depends on a companion clabwire-capture PR.

**Suggested correction:** Either ship the `capture` command in this PR, drop the `capture` item from the FOR loop with a comment noting the dependency, or skip that individual item when the tested binary lacks the command so the remaining release-gate assertions still run.


## Coverage

- Source-only review of a read-only snapshot; no tests, formatters, or linters were executed. Go and robot suites were reviewed statically.
- All 25 manifest paths examined via `diff.txt` plus targeted head-file reads; the diff tail beyond line ~3861 was covered by reading the head files directly &#40;both robot suites, docs, [`reconcile.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/labruntime/clabernetes/reconcile.go#L1-L1), [`labruntime_access.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/core/labruntime_access.go#L1-L1), [`cmd/root.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/cmd/root.go#L1-L1)&#41;.
- Resolved candidates&#58; `${lab-namespace}` in [`02-release-check.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/tests/14-clabernetes/02-release-check.robot#L1-L1) is a deliberate literal matching [`01-linux-lifecycle.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/tests/14-clabernetes/01-linux-lifecycle.robot#L1-L1); `stop -n` shorthand exists in [`cmd/stop.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/cmd/stop.go#L1-L1); `events --format json` is valid; `CLAB_KUBECONFIG` exists in [`clabernetes.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/labruntime/clabernetes/clabernetes.go#L1-L1) and docs; documented error text matches [`support.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/labruntime/clabernetes/support.go#L1-L1); the `spec.labels` removal in [`primitives.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/labruntime/clabernetes/primitives.go#L1-L1) is intentional and tested in [`nodes_test.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/labruntime/clabernetes/nodes_test.go#L1-L1); the connect early-return cannot skip the support check because views are copies whose ensure already ran at creation.
- The `OpenAPI` check itself is covered by `TestCheckNodeRunStateSchema`, `TestSupportCheckRunsOnceBeforeTheFirstClusterCall`, `TestSupportCheckRetriesFailedRequestsAndRemembersSuccess`, and `TestSupportCheckReadsTheOpenAPIDocumentAsTheCaller`; the robot suite&#39;s behavior against a real 0.10.1 CRD cluster was verified by inspection only since it needs an external cluster.

1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)
</content>

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

215: -corresponding Node labels. A grouped secondary shares lifecycle with its

217: -
218: -`restart` patches each selected Deployment with a restart annotation and waits

224: +(`"Running"` for `start`). `stop` returns once the controller reports the

227: +the node's readiness is `ready`. Both wait at most `--timeout`.
228: +
229: +`restart` sets a new token in the `c9s.run/restart-requested` annotation of the
230: +node. The controller replaces the Pod once per new token, and `restart` returns
231: +when `status.observedRestartToken` equals the token and the node is ready. A
232: +stopped node is started by the same patch.
233: +
234: +What a stopped node keeps and loses:
235: +
236: +- The `Node`, its Services, PersistentVolumeClaims and Links stay. Saved
237: +  configuration survives a stop and start.
238: +- Its links go carrier-down on every peer, like an unplugged cable;
239: +  `events` reports them as interface `down` events.
240: +- `inspect` shows the node as `stopped` (`stopping` while its Pod terminates).
241: +- clabernetes keeps a running peer of a stopped node `notready`: its
242: +  connectivity sidecar waits for the far end of the wire. Deploy, apply, start
243: +  and restart treat such a node as settled when its containers are ready, and
244: +  log `link peers stopped: <nodes>` instead of waiting for it.
245: +
246: +Nodes that share a Pod (`network-mode: container:<node>`) follow the run state
247: +of their primary node. Stopping, starting or restarting any node of the group
248: +acts on the primary, once.
249: +
250: +The controllers keep reconciling while nodes are stopped. A `deploy` that
251: +changes a stopped node updates its `Node`; the node stays stopped and boots the
252: +new definition on its next `start`. Containerlab never sends `spec.runState`
253: +during deploy, and with `--no-topology-cr` it carries the run state of existing
254: +Nodes over, so an apply never starts a stopped node.

A stopped node's links go carrier-down on\n-every peer, exactly like unplugging a cable.\n-\n-`start` scales the selected Deployments back to `1` and clears the\n-corresponding Node labels. A grouped secondary shares lifecycle with its\n-primary node's Deployment.\n-\n-`restart` patches each selected Deployment with a restart annotation and waits\n-for it to become ready:\n-\n-```text\n-kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=<utc timestamp>\n-```\n+(`\"Running\"` for `start`). `stop` returns once the controller reports the\n+`Stopped` condition as `True`, which it does when no Pod of the node remains.\n+`start` returns once the condition is `False` for the patched generation and\n+the node's readiness is `ready`. The controller replaces the Pod once per new token, and `restart` returns\n+when `status.observedRestartToken` equals the token and the node is ready. A\n+stopped node is started by the same patch.\n+\n+What a stopped node keeps and loses:\n+\n+- The `Node`, its Services, PersistentVolumeClaims and Links stay. Saved\n+  configuration survives a stop and start.\n+- Its links go carrier-down on every peer, like an unplugged cable;\n+  `events` reports them as interface `down` events.\n+- `inspect` shows the node as `stopped` (`stopping` while its Pod terminates).\n+- clabernetes keeps a running peer of a stopped node `notready`: its\n+  connectivity sidecar waits for the far end of the wire. 1807: +		},

1811: +			"conditions": []any{map[string]any{

1819: +// fakeNodeController plays the clabernetes Node controller in the dynamic fake: a patch bumps
1820: +// the Node generation like the API server does for spec changes, and after lag reads of a Node
1821: +// the controller reports the requested run state and restart token in its status.
1822: +type fakeNodeController struct {
1823: +	t       *testing.T
1824: +	tracker k8stesting.ObjectTracker
1825: +	lag     int
1826: +
1827: +	// peers are the link peers of each node; a running node with a stopped peer stays not
1828: +	// ready with ready containers, as clabernetes reports it
1829: +	peers map[string][]string
1830: +
1831: +	mu      sync.Mutex
1832: +	reads   map[string]int
1833: +	patches []k8stesting.PatchAction
1834: +}
1835: +
1836: +func newFakeNodeController(t *testing.T, r *Runtime, lag int) *fakeNodeController {
1837: +	t.Helper()
1838: +
1839: +	client := r.client.(*dynamicfake.FakeDynamicClient)
1840: +	controller := &fakeNodeController{
1841: +		t: t, tracker: client.Tracker(), lag: lag, reads: map[string]int{},
1842: +	}
1843: +	client.PrependReactor("patch", "nodes", controller.patch)
1844: +	client.PrependReactor("get", "nodes", controller.get)
1845: +
1846: +	return controller
1847: +}
1848: +
1849: +func (c *fakeNodeController) patch(action k8stesting.Action) (bool, k8sruntime.Object, error) {
1850: +	patch := action.(k8stesting.PatchAction)
1851: +
1852: +	c.mu.Lock()
1853: +	c.patches = append(c.patches, patch)
1854: +	c.reads[patch.GetName()] = 0
1855: +	c.mu.Unlock()
1856: +
1857: +	var body map[string]any
1858: +	if err := json.Unmarshal(patch.GetPatch(), &body); err != nil {
1859: +		c.t.Errorf("patch is not JSON: %v", err)
1860: +	}
1861: +	if _, changesSpec := body["spec"]; changesSpec {
1862: +		obj, err := c.tracker.Get(nodeGVR, patch.GetNamespace(), patch.GetName())
1863: +		if err != nil {
1864: +			return true, nil, err
1865: +		}
1866: +		node := obj.(*unstructured.Unstructured)
1867: +		node.SetGeneration(node.GetGeneration() + 1)
1868: +		if err := c.tracker.Update(nodeGVR, node, patch.GetNamespace()); err != nil {
1869: +			return true, nil, err
1870: +		}
1871: +	}
1872: +
1873: +	// the default reaction applies the patch
1874: +	return false, nil, nil
1875: +}
1876: +
1877: +func (c *fakeNodeController) get(action k8stesting.Action) (bool, k8sruntime.Object, error) {
1878: +	get := action.(k8stesting.GetAction)
1879: +
1880: +	c.mu.Lock()
1881: +	c.reads[get.GetName()]++
1882: +	reconcile := c.reads[get.GetName()] > c.lag
1883: +	c.mu.Unlock()
1884: +	if !reconcile {
1885: +		return false, nil, nil
1886: +	}
1887: +
1888: +	obj, err := c.tracker.Get(nodeGVR, get.GetNamespace(), get.GetName())
1889: +	if err != nil {
1890: +		return false, nil, nil //nolint:nilerr // the default reaction reports it
1891: +	}
1892: +	node := obj.(*unstructured.Unstructured).DeepCopy()
1893: +
1894: +	status := map[string]any{"readiness": nodeReadinessReady}
1895: +	condition := map[string]any{
1896: +		"type": nodeConditionStopped, "status": "False", "reason": "Running",
1897: +		"observedGeneration": node.GetGeneration(),
1898: +	}
1899: +	containers := map[string]any{"type": nodeConditionContainersReady, "status": "True"}
1900: +	if nodeRunState(node) == nodeRunStateStopped {
1901: +		status["readiness"] = "notready"
1902: +		condition["status"], condition["reason"] = "True", "Stopped"
1903: +		containers["status"] = "Unknown"
1904: +	}
1905: +	for _, peer := range c.peers[node.GetName()] {
1906: +		peerObj, err := c.tracker.Get(nodeGVR, get.GetNamespace(), peer)
1907: +		if err == nil && nodeRunState(peerObj.(*unstructured.Unstructured)) == nodeRunStateStopped {
1908: +			status["readiness"] = "notready"
1909: +		}
1910: +	}
1911: +	status["conditions"] = []any{condition, containers}
1912: +	if token := node.GetAnnotations()[restartRequestedAnnotation]; token != "" &&
1913: +		nodeRunState(node) != nodeRunStateStopped {
1914: +		status["observedRestartToken"] = token
1915: +	}
1916: +	node.Object["status"] = status
1917: +	if err := c.tracker.Update(nodeGVR, node, get.GetNamespace()); err != nil {
1918: +		c.t.Errorf("update status: %v", err)
1919: +	}
1920: +
1921: +	return false, nil, nil
1922: +}
1923: +
1924: +func (c *fakeNodeController) patchBodies() map[string]map[string]any {
1925: +	c.mu.Lock()
1926: +	defer c.mu.Unlock()
1927: +
1928: +	bodies := map[string]map[string]any{}
1929: +	for _, patch := range c.patches {
1930: +		if patch.GetPatchType() != "application/merge-patch+json" {
1931: +			c.t.Errorf("patch type = %s, want a merge patch", patch.GetPatchType())
1932: +		}
1933: +		var body map[string]any
1934: +		_ = json.Unmarshal(patch.GetPatch(), &body)
1935: +		bodies[patch.GetName()] = body
1936: +	}
1937: +
1938: +	return bodies
1939: +}

1943: +func runStateTestRuntime(t *testing.T, lag int) (*Runtime, *fakeNodeController) {

1945: +
1946: +	r := newTestRuntime(
1947: +		runStateTestNode("r1", nil),

1950: +	)

1957: +func assertNoWorkloadAccess(t *testing.T, r *Runtime) {
1958: +	t.Helper()
1959: +
1960: +	for _, action := range r.kubeClient.(*kubefake.Clientset).Actions() {
1961: +		if action.GetResource().Group == "apps" ||
1962: +			(action.GetResource().Resource == "pods" && action.GetVerb() != "list" &&
1963: +				action.GetVerb() != "get" && action.GetVerb() != "watch") {
1964: +			t.Fatalf("node lifecycle touched workloads: %s %s", action.GetVerb(),
1965: +				action.GetResource())
1966: +		}
1967: +	}
1968: +	for _, action := range r.client.(*dynamicfake.FakeDynamicClient).Actions() {
1969: +		if action.GetResource().Resource == "topologies" && action.GetVerb() != "get" &&
1970: +			action.GetVerb() != "list" {
1971: +			t.Fatalf("node lifecycle changed the Topology: %s", action.GetVerb())
1972: +		}
1973: +		if action.GetVerb() == "update" {
1974: +			t.Fatalf("node lifecycle updated %s instead of patching it", action.GetResource())
1975: +		}
1976: +	}
1977: +}

1979: +func TestStopPatchesThePrimaryRunStateAndWaitsForStopped(t *testing.T) {
1980: +	t.Parallel()
1981: +
1982: +	r, controller := runStateTestRuntime(t, 3)
1983: +
1984: +	// r2b shares the pod of r2, so stopping it stops r2, once
1985: +	err := r.Stop(context.Background(), clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
1986: +		Name: "lab1", Nodes: []string{"R2B", "r2"},
1987: +	})
1988: +	if err != nil {
1989: +		t.Fatal(err)
1990: +	}
1991: +
1992: +	bodies := controller.patchBodies()
1993: +	if len(bodies) != 1 {
1994: +		t.Fatalf("patched nodes = %v, want only the primary r2", bodies)
1995: +	}
1996: +	want := `{"spec":{"runState":"Stopped"}}`
1997: +	if got, _ := json.Marshal(bodies["r2"]); string(got) != want {
1998: +		t.Fatalf("stop patch = %s, want %s", got, want)
1999: +	}
2000: +
2001: +	node := getTestPrimitive(t, r, nodeGVR, "lab-ns", "r2")
2002: +	condition := nodeCondition(node, nodeConditionStopped)
2003: +	if condition == nil || condition.status != "True" {
2004: +		t.Fatalf("Stop returned before the controller reported Stopped: %+v", node.Object["status"])
2005: +	}
2006: +	assertNoWorkloadAccess(t, r)
2007: +
2008: +	// the state reports the group as stopped
2009: +	state := &clablabruntime.LabState{Name: "lab1", Namespace: "lab-ns"}
2010: +	if err := r.enrichState(context.Background(), state); err != nil {
2011: +		t.Fatal(err)
2012: +	}
2013: +	states := map[string]string{}
2014: +	for _, n := range state.Nodes {
2015: +		states[n.Name] = n.State
2016: +	}
2017: +	if states["r2"] != "stopped" || states["r2b"] != "stopped" || states["r1"] != "ready" {
2018: +		t.Fatalf("node states = %v, want r2 and r2b stopped, r1 ready", states)
2019: +	}
2020: +}

2060: +func TestRestartSetsANewTokenAndWaitsForIt(t *testing.T) {
2061: +	t.Parallel()
2062: +
2063: +	r, controller := runStateTestRuntime(t, 2)
2064: +	ctx := context.Background()
2065: +
2066: +	if err := r.Restart(
2067: +		ctx,

2069: +	); err != nil {
2070: +		t.Fatal(err)
2071: +	}
2072: +	first := controller.patchBodies()["r1"]
2073: +	metadata, _ := first["metadata"].(map[string]any)
2074: +	annotations, _ := metadata["annotations"].(map[string]any)
2075: +	token, _ := annotations[restartRequestedAnnotation].(string)
2076: +	if token == "" || first["spec"] != nil {
2077: +		t.Fatalf("restart patch = %v, want only the restart-requested annotation", first)
2078: +	}
2079: +	node := getTestPrimitive(t, r, nodeGVR, "lab-ns", "r1")
2080: +	if observed, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(
2081: +		node.Object, "status", "observedRestartToken",
2082: +	); observed != token {
2083: +		t.Fatalf("Restart returned before the token was observed: %q, want %q", observed, token)
2084: +	}
2085: +	if strings.Contains(string(mustJSON(t, first)), "restart-tokens") {
2086: +		t.Fatal("the restart patch set the controller-owned restart-tokens annotation")
2087: +	}
2088: +
2089: +	// a stopped node is started by the restart patch, with a different token
2090: +	if err := r.Stop(
2091: +		ctx,
2092: +		clablabruntime.NodeRequest{Name: "lab1", Nodes: []string{"r2"}},
2093: +	); err != nil {
2094: +		t.Fatal(err)
2095: +	}
2096: +	if err := r.Restart(
2097: +		ctx,
2098: +		clablabruntime.NodeRequest{Name: "lab1", Nodes: []string{"r2b"}},
2099: +	); err != nil {
2100: +		t.Fatal(err)
2101: +	}
2102: +	second := controller.patchBodies()["r2"]
2103: +	spec, _ := second["spec"].(map[string]any)
2104: +	if spec["runState"] != nodeRunStateRunning {
2105: +		t.Fatalf("restart of a stopped node = %v, want runState Running", second)
2106: +	}
2107: +	secondToken := second["metadata"].(map[string]any)["annotations"].(map[string]any)[restartRequestedAnnotation]
2108: +	if secondToken == token {
2109: +		t.Fatal("two restarts used the same token")
2110: +	}

2539: +func TestPrimitiveObjectsConformAfterAnAPIRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
2540: +	t.Parallel()
2541: +
2542: +	req := manifestsTestRequest(t)
2543: +	req.NoTopologyCR = true
2544: +	req.Namespace = "lab-ns"
2545: +	prepared, err := prepareDesiredDeployment(context.Background(), req, "lab-ns")
2546: +	if err != nil {
2547: +		t.Fatal(err)
2548: +	}
2549: +
2550: +	for _, group := range prepared.primitives.groups() {
2551: +		for _, obj := range group.objects {
2552: +			stored := &unstructured.Unstructured{}
2553: +			if err := stored.UnmarshalJSON(mustJSON(t, obj.Object)); err != nil {
2554: +				t.Fatal(err)
2555: +			}
2556: +			if group.kind == "Node" {
2557: +				// the API server defaults the run state and prunes fields the schema lacks
2558: +				_ = unstructured.SetNestedField(
2559: +					stored.Object,
2560: +					nodeRunStateRunning,
2561: +					"spec",
2562: +					"runState",
2563: +				)
2564: +				unstructured.RemoveNestedField(stored.Object, "spec", "labels")
2565: +				if obj.GetLabels()[labelOriginalNodeName] == "" {
2566: +					t.Errorf("Node %s lost its %s label", obj.GetName(), labelOriginalNodeName)
2567: +				}
2568: +			}
2569: +			if !primitiveObjectsConform(stored, reconciledPrimitiveObject(stored, obj)) {
2570: +				t.Errorf("%s %s drifts after an API round trip", group.kind, obj.GetName())
2571: +			}
2572: +		}
2573: +	}
2574: +}

3079: +			return resolveOpenAPIRef(doc, property), true
3080: +		}
3081: +		switch {
3082: +		case schema.Ref != "":
3083: +			schema = resolveOpenAPIRef(doc, schema)
3084: +		case len(schema.AllOf) == 1:
3085: +			schema = resolveOpenAPIRef(doc, schema.AllOf[0])
3086: +		default:
3087: +			return openAPISchema{}, false
3088: +		}
3089: +	}
3090: +
3091: +	return openAPISchema{}, false
3092: +}
3093: +
3094: +func resolveOpenAPIRef(doc openAPIDocument, schema openAPISchema) openAPISchema {
3095: +	for range 8 {
3096: +		switch {
3097: +		case schema.Ref != "":
3098: +			name := strings.TrimPrefix(schema.Ref, "#/components/schemas/")
3099: +			resolved, ok := doc.Components.Schemas[name]
3100: +			if !ok {
3101: +				return schema
3102: +			}
3103: +			schema = resolved
3104: +		case len(schema.AllOf) == 1 && len(schema.Properties) == 0:
3105: +			schema = schema.AllOf[0]
3106: +		default:
3107: +			return schema
3108: +		}
3109: +	}
3110: +
3111: +	return schema
3112: +}
3113: +
3114: +// CheckSupport checks that the cluster runs a clabernetes release with the contract the c9s
3115: +// runtime needs, and returns an error wrapping labruntime.ErrUnsupportedRuntimeVersion that
3116: +// names the required release when it does not. Every cluster operation runs the same check
3117: +// once per runtime instance; servers call it at startup to fail early.
3118: +func (r *Runtime) CheckSupport(ctx context.Context, identity clablabruntime.Identity) error {
3119: +	_, err := r.connect(ctx, identity)
3120: +
3121: +	return err
3122: +}

3704: @@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
3705: +*** Comments ***
3706: +The c9s runtime refuses clusters whose clabernetes release lacks Node run state and the clabwire
3707: +capture contract. This suite needs a second cluster that serves the older c9s.run CRDs (for
3708: +example a KinD cluster with only the clabernetes 0.10.1 CRDs applied); set
3709: +CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG to its kubeconfig. Without it, the suite is skipped.
3710: +
3711: +
3712: +*** Settings ***
3713: +Library             OperatingSystem
3714: +Library             Process
3715: +Resource            ../common.robot
3716: +
3717: +Suite Setup         Setup
3718: +Test Tags           clabernetes    c9s
3719: +
3720: +
3721: +*** Variables ***
3722: +${runtime}          c9s
3723: +${topo}             ${CURDIR}/01-linux-lifecycle.clab.yml
3724: +${lab-namespace}    c9s-c9s-linux-lifecycle
3725: +${required}         clabernetes with Node run state and the clabwire capture contract (0.11 or newer)
3726: +
3727: +
3728: +*** Test Cases ***
3729: +Cluster commands fail before the first cluster call
3730: +    FOR    ${args}    IN
3731: +    ...    inspect --all
3732: +    ...    deploy -t ${topo}
3733: +    ...    stop -t ${topo} -n server
3734: +    ...    capture -t ${topo} --list
3735: +    ...    events --format json
3736: +        ${output} =    Run Old Cluster Command    ${args}
3737: +        Should Not Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
3738: +        # the error box wraps long lines
3739: +        ${message} =    Evaluate    " ".join($output.stderr.split())
3740: +        Should Contain    ${message}    no spec.runState
3741: +        Should Contain    ${message}    ${required}
3742: +    END
3743: +
3744: +    ${namespace} =    Process.Run Process
3745: +    ...    kubectl --kubeconfig %{CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG} get namespace ${lab-namespace} --ignore-not-found -o name
3746: +    ...    shell=True
3747: +    Should Be Empty    ${namespace.stdout}
3748: +
3749: +Offline commands skip the check
3750: +    ${validate} =    Run Old Cluster Command    validate -t ${topo}
3751: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${validate.rc}    0
3752: +
3753: +    ${emit} =    Run Old Cluster Command    deploy -t ${topo} --emit-crs
3754: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${emit.rc}    0
3755: +    Should Contain    ${emit.stdout}    kind: Topology
3756: +
3757: +
3758: +*** Keywords ***
3759: +Setup
3760: +    Skip If    '${runtime}' != 'c9s'    This suite targets the c9s runtime.
3761: +    ${old} =    Get Environment Variable    CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG    ${EMPTY}
3762: +    Skip If    '${old}' == ''    CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG is not set
3763: +
3764: +Run Old Cluster Command
3765: +    [Arguments]    ${args}
3766: +    ${output} =    Process.Run Process
3767: +    ...    ${CLAB_BIN} --runtime ${runtime} ${args}
3768: +    ...    shell=True
3769: +    ...    timeout=60s
3770: +    ...    env:KUBECONFIG=%{CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG}
3771: +    ...    env:CLAB_KUBECONFIG=%{CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG}
3772: +    Log    stdout:${\n}${output.stdout}    console=${True}
3773: +    Log    stderr:${\n}${output.stderr}    console=${True}
3774: +    RETURN    ${output}

16: // The helpers in this file give library users per-node access to the lab selected by the CLab
17: // (its topology file or WithTopologyName). Node names are accepted as the topology file spells
18: // them or as a lab runtime sanitized them. Lab runtime calls act as the identity set with
19: // WithLabRuntimeIdentity.
20: 
21: // CheckLabRuntimeSupport checks that the cluster behind the lab runtime runs a controller release
22: // with the contract the runtime needs (for c9s: clabernetes with Node run state and the clabwire
23: // capture contract). Lab runtime operations run the same check before their first cluster call;
24: // servers call it to fail early. The error wraps labruntime.ErrUnsupportedRuntimeVersion when the
25: // release is too old.
26: func (c *CLab) CheckLabRuntimeSupport(ctx context.Context) error {
27: 	checker, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.SupportChecker](
28: 		c, "checking the lab runtime version")
29: 	if err != nil {
30: 		return err
31: 	}
32: 
33: 	return checker.CheckSupport(ctx, c.labRuntimeIdentity)
34: }
35: 
36: // LocateLabRuntimeNodes reports the workload (namespace, pod, primary device container, Node
37: // UID, exposed ports) of the given nodes, or of every node of the lab when none are given.
38: func (c *CLab) LocateLabRuntimeNodes(
39: 	ctx context.Context,
40: 	nodeNames ...string,
41: ) ([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, error) {
42: 	locator, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLocator](c, "locating nodes")
43: 	if err != nil {
44: 		return nil, err
45: 	}
46: 	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
47: 		return nil, err
48: 	}
49: 
50: 	return locator.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
51: 		Name:     c.Config.Name,
52: 		Nodes:    nodeNames,
53: 		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
54: 	})
55: }
56: 
57: // AttachLabRuntimeNode runs an interactive command in a node's device container (or in
58: // req.Container) with stdin, an optional TTY and terminal resizing. The lab name and identity
59: // default to the CLab's. A command exiting nonzero returns a *labruntime.CommandExitError.
60: func (c *CLab) AttachLabRuntimeNode(
61: 	ctx context.Context,
62: 	req clablabruntime.AttachRequest,
63: 	streams clablabruntime.AttachStreams,
64: ) error {
65: 	attacher, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeAttacher](c, "attaching to nodes")
66: 	if err != nil {
67: 		return err
68: 	}
69: 
70: 	if req.Name == "" {
71: 		if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
72: 			return err
73: 		}
74: 		req.Name = c.Config.Name
75: 	}
76: 	if req.Identity.IsZero() {
77: 		req.Identity = c.labRuntimeIdentity
78: 	}
79: 
80: 	return attacher.Attach(ctx, req, streams)
81: }

84: // lab runtime, such as a Kubernetes port-forward.
85: func (c *CLab) DialLabRuntimeNodePort(
86: 	ctx context.Context,
87: 	nodeName string,
88: 	port int,
89: ) (net.Conn, error) {
90: 	forwarder, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodePortForwarder](
91: 		c, "port-forwarding to nodes")
92: 	if err != nil {
93: 		return nil, err
94: 	}
95: 	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
96: 		return nil, err
97: 	}
98: 
99: 	return forwarder.DialPort(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
100: 		Name:     c.Config.Name,
101: 		Nodes:    []string{nodeName},
102: 		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
103: 	}, port)
104: }

125: // NodeLogOptions selects the node log NodeLogs writes.
126: type NodeLogOptions struct {

128: 	NodeName string
129: 	// Container overrides a lab runtime node's primary device container. Local runtimes do

140: // NodeLogs writes the log of a lab node with every runtime: the container log with Docker and

142: // stdout.

146: 	stdout, stderr io.Writer,

149: 		return fmt.Errorf("node name is required")
150: 	}
151: 	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
152: 		return err
153: 	}
154: 
155: 	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
156: 		streamer, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLogStreamer](
157: 			c, "streaming node logs")
158: 		if err != nil {
159: 			return err
160: 		}
161: 
162: 		return streamer.StreamLogs(ctx, clablabruntime.LogRequest{
163: 			Name:       c.Config.Name,
164: 			NodeName:   opts.NodeName,
165: 			Container:  opts.Container,
166: 			Tail:       opts.Tail,
167: 			Follow:     opts.Follow,
168: 			Timestamps: opts.Timestamps,
169: 			Identity:   c.labRuntimeIdentity,
170: 		}, stdout)
171: 	}
172: 
173: 	if opts.Container != "" {
174: 		return fmt.Errorf("selecting a container is only supported with lab runtimes")
175: 	}
176: 
177: 	runtime, containerName, err := c.nodeContainer(ctx, opts.NodeName)
178: 	if err != nil {
179: 		return err
180: 	}
181: 
182: 	writer, ok := runtime.(clabruntime.ContainerLogWriter)
183: 	if !ok {
184: 		return fmt.Errorf("container runtime %q does not support node logs", runtime.GetName())
185: 	}
186: 
187: 	return writer.WriteContainerLogs(ctx, containerName, clabruntime.ContainerLogOptions{
188: 		Tail:       opts.Tail,
189: 		Follow:     opts.Follow,
190: 		Timestamps: opts.Timestamps,
191: 	}, stdout, stderr)
192: }
193: 
194: // nodeContainer finds the container of a lab node in the local container runtimes by the lab
195: // and node name labels.
196: func (c *CLab) nodeContainer(
197: 	ctx context.Context,
198: 	nodeName string,
199: ) (clabruntime.ContainerRuntime, string, error) {
200: 	filters := []*clabtypes.GenericFilter{
201: 		{
202: 			FilterType: "label",
203: 			Field:      clabconstants.Containerlab,
204: 			Operator:   "=",
205: 			Match:      c.Config.Name,
206: 		},
207: 		{
208: 			FilterType: "label",
209: 			Field:      clabconstants.NodeName,
210: 			Operator:   "=",
211: 			Match:      nodeName,
212: 		},
213: 	}
214: 
215: 	runtimeNames := make([]string, 0, len(c.Runtimes))
216: 	for name := range c.Runtimes {
217: 		runtimeNames = append(runtimeNames, name)
218: 	}
219: 	sort.Strings(runtimeNames)
220: 
221: 	for _, name := range runtimeNames {
222: 		runtime := c.Runtimes[name]
223: 
224: 		containers, err := runtime.ListContainers(ctx, filters)
225: 		if err != nil {
226: 			return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("could not list containers: %w", err)
227: 		}
228: 		if len(containers) != 0 && len(containers[0].Names) != 0 {
229: 			return runtime, containers[0].Names[0], nil
230: 		}
231: 	}
232: 
233: 	return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("%w: node %q of lab %q has no container",
234: 		ErrNodeNotFound, nodeName, c.Config.Name)
235: }
236: 
237: func (c *CLab) requireLabName() error {
238: 	if c.Config == nil || c.Config.Name == "" {
239: 		return fmt.Errorf("provide a lab name (--name) or a topology file (--topo)")
240: 	}
241: 
242: 	return nil
243: }
244: 
245: // labRuntimeCapability returns the CLab's lab runtime as an optional lab runtime interface.
246: func labRuntimeCapability[T any](c *CLab, operation string) (T, error) {
247: 	var zero T
248: 
249: 	if c.LabRuntime == nil {
250: 		return zero, fmt.Errorf("%s needs a lab runtime such as %q",
251: 			operation, clablabruntime.ClabernetesRuntimeName)
252: 	}
253: 
254: 	capability, ok := c.LabRuntime.(T)
255: 	if !ok {
256: 		return zero, fmt.Errorf("lab runtime %q does not support %s",
257: 			c.globalRuntimeName, operation)
258: 	}
259: 
260: 	return capability, nil
261: }

137: // newestPod prefers a running pod and, among equals, the newest one: several pods can match a
138: // node during a rolling update.
139: func newestPod(current, candidate *corev1.Pod) *corev1.Pod {
140: 	if current == nil {
141: 		return candidate
142: 	}
143: 
144: 	currentRunning := current.Status.Phase == corev1.PodRunning
145: 	candidateRunning := candidate.Status.Phase == corev1.PodRunning
146: 	if currentRunning != candidateRunning {
147: 		if candidateRunning {
148: 			return candidate
149: 		}
150: 
151: 		return current
152: 	}
153: 
154: 	if candidate.CreationTimestamp.After(current.CreationTimestamp.Time) {
155: 		return candidate
156: 	}
157: 
158: 	return current
159: }

161: func (r *Runtime) enrichState(ctx context.Context, state *clablabruntime.LabState) error {
162: 	if state == nil || state.Name == "" {
163: 		return nil
164: 	}
165: 
166: 	nodeResources, err := r.nodesForTopology(ctx, state.Name, state.Namespace)
167: 	if err != nil {
168: 		return err
169: 	}
170: 
171: 	nodesByName := map[string]clablabruntime.NodeState{}
172: 	for _, node := range state.Nodes {
173: 		nodesByName[node.Name] = node
174: 	}
175: 
176: 	networkModes := make(map[string]string, len(nodeResources.Items))
177: 	resourcesByName := make(map[string]*unstructured.Unstructured, len(nodeResources.Items))
178: 	for idx := range nodeResources.Items {
179: 		nodeResource := &nodeResources.Items[idx]
180: 		nodesByName[nodeResource.GetName()] = nodeStateFromResource(nodeResource)
181: 		networkModes[nodeResource.GetName()] = nodeNetworkMode(nodeResource)
182: 		resourcesByName[nodeResource.GetName()] = nodeResource
183: 	}
184: 
185: 	pods, err := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().Pods(state.Namespace).List(ctx, metav1.ListOptions{
186: 		LabelSelector: labels.Set{
187: 			labelApp:           clabernetesAppValue,
188: 			labelTopologyOwner: state.Name,
189: 		}.String(),
190: 	})
191: 	if err != nil {
192: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to list clabernetes pods for topology %s/%s: %w",
193: 			state.Namespace, state.Name, err)
194: 	}
195: 
196: 	podsByNode := map[string]*corev1.Pod{}
197: 	for idx := range pods.Items {
198: 		nodeName := pods.Items[idx].Labels[labelTopologyNode]
199: 		if nodeName == "" {
200: 			continue
201: 		}
202: 		podsByNode[nodeName] = newestPod(podsByNode[nodeName], &pods.Items[idx])
203: 	}
204: 
205: 	// The Node's status.readiness is the authoritative device signal. The primary Node's run
206: 	// state governs the pod a group of nodes shares: a stopped primary stops the whole group.
207: 	// Nodes without readiness yet report their pod phase.
208: 	for nodeName, node := range nodesByName {
209: 		primary := resolvePrimaryNode(nodeName, networkModes)
210: 		if primaryResource := resourcesByName[primary]; primaryResource != nil &&
211: 			nodeRunState(primaryResource) == nodeRunStateStopped {
212: 			node.State = "stopping"
213: 			if condition := nodeCondition(
214: 				primaryResource,
215: 				nodeConditionStopped,
216: 			); condition != nil &&
217: 				condition.status == string(metav1.ConditionTrue) {
218: 				node.State = "stopped"
219: 			}
220: 			node.Ready = false
221: 		} else if pod := podsByNode[primary]; node.State == "" && pod != nil &&
222: 			pod.Status.Phase != "" {
223: 			node.State = strings.ToLower(string(pod.Status.Phase))
224: 		}
225: 		nodesByName[nodeName] = node
226: 	}
227: 
228: 	// Nodes grouped through network-mode container: share the pod of the group's primary
229: 	// node. Before the controller observed the device containers, the pod's default-container
230: 	// annotation names the primary node's container.
231: 	for nodeName, node := range nodesByName {
232: 		primary := resolvePrimaryNode(nodeName, networkModes)
233: 		pod := podsByNode[primary]
234: 		if pod == nil {
235: 			continue
236: 		}
237: 
238: 		node.Pod = pod.Name
239: 		if node.Container == "" && primary == nodeName {
240: 			node.Container = pod.Annotations[defaultContainerAnnotation]
241: 		}
242: 		nodesByName[nodeName] = node
243: 	}
244: 
245: 	nodeNames := make([]string, 0, len(nodesByName))
246: 	for nodeName := range nodesByName {
247: 		nodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)
248: 	}
249: 	sort.Strings(nodeNames)
250: 
251: 	state.Nodes = make([]clablabruntime.NodeState, 0, len(nodeNames))
252: 	allReady := len(nodeNames) > 0 // codespell:ignore allready
253: 	allStopped := len(nodeNames) > 0
254: 	for _, nodeName := range nodeNames {
255: 		node := nodesByName[nodeName]
256: 		state.Nodes = append(state.Nodes, node)
257: 		allReady = allReady && node.Ready // codespell:ignore allready
258: 		allStopped = allStopped && node.State == "stopped"
259: 	}
260: 
261: 	switch {
262: 	case allReady: // codespell:ignore allready
263: 		state.State = "running"
264: 		state.Ready = true
265: 	case allStopped:
266: 		state.State = "stopped"
267: 		state.Ready = false
268: 	case len(nodeNames) != 0:
269: 		state.State = "partial"
270: 		state.Ready = false
271: 	}
272: 
273: 	return nil

- Tests: new `labruntime/clabernetes/nodes_test.go` (e.g. `TestCheckNodeRunStateSchema`, `TestSupportCheckRunsOnceBeforeTheFirstClusterCall`), modified `clabernetes_test.go` (`TestDeployReconcilesPrimitiveResources` asserts run-state carry-over and restart annotation preserved; removed Deployment rollout tests). <content>
1: package clabernetes
2: 
3: import (
4: 	"context"
5: 	"encoding/json"
6: 	"fmt"
7: 	"strings"
8: 	"sync"
9: 
10: 	clablabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime"
11: 	apierrors "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/errors"
12: )
13: 
14: // requiredClabernetes names the clabernetes release the runtime needs. Node run state
15: // (nodes.c9s.run spec.runState with restart requests) and the clabwire capture contract
16: // (--nodeName, repeated --interface, --format pcapng, --list-interfaces) ship together, so one
17: // check of the run state field covers both.
18: const requiredClabernetes = "clabernetes with Node run state and the clabwire capture contract " +
19: 	"(0.11 or newer)"
20: 
21: // c9sOpenAPIPath is the OpenAPI v3 document of the c9s.run/v1alpha1 group. The API server
22: // publishes the CRD schemas there, and every authenticated user may read it (system:discovery),
23: // so users bound only to the clabernetes lab roles can run the check. Reading the CRD itself
24: // would need cluster-scoped RBAC.
25: const c9sOpenAPIPath = "/openapi/v3/apis/c9s.run/v1alpha1"
26: 
27: // supportCheck runs the clabernetes version check once per runtime instance. A cluster that
28: // lacks the contract is remembered as such; a failed request is retried on the next call.
29: type supportCheck struct {
30: 	// fetch returns the OpenAPI v3 document of the c9s.run/v1alpha1 group; nil reads it from
31: 	// the API server.
32: 	fetch func(ctx context.Context, r *Runtime) ([]byte, error)
33:

222: 	}

  Line 4:   - Packet capture

  Line 8: # Packet capture & Wireshark

  Line 16: Containerlab offers a simple way to capture the packets from any interface of any node in the lab. This article will explain how to do that.

  Line 20: If you are looking for a free Web UI for packet capture with Wireshark, check out our [Edgeshark integration](#edgeshark-integration).

  Line 23: Consider the following lab topology which highlights the typical points of packet capture.

  Line 30: ## Packet capture, namespaces and interfaces

  Line 32: To capture the packets from a given interface requires having that interface's name and its network namespace (netns). And that's it.

  Line 51: - local capture: when the capture is started from the containerlab host itself.

  Line 52: - remote capture: when the capture is started from a remote machine that connects via SSH to the containerlab host and starts the capture.

  Line 56: ### local capture

  Line 58: Local capture assumes the capture is initiated from the containerlab host. For instance, to capture from the `e1-1` interface of the `clab-quickstart-srl` node use:

  Line 64: In this example we first entered the namespace where the target interface is located using `ip netns exec` command and then started the capture with `tcpdump` providing the interface name to it.

  Line 66: The downside of local capture is that typically containerlab hosts run in a headless (no UI) mode and thus the visibility of the captured traffic is limited to the console output. This is where `tshark` might come in in handy by providing more readable output. Still, the lack of Wireshark UI is a downside, therefore it is our recommendation for you to get familiar with the remote capture method.

  Line 68: ### remote capture

  Line 70: The limitations of the local capture are lifted when the remote capture is used. In the remote capture model you initiate the packet capture from your descktop/laptop and the traffic is sent to your machine where it can be displayed in the Wireshark UI.

  Line 72: Before we start mixing in the Wireshark, lets see how the remote capture is initiated:

  Line 79: Assuming we ran the above command from our laptop, we rely on `$containerlab_host_address` being reachable from our laptop. We use `ssh` to connect to the remote containerlab host and execute the same command we did in the local capture.  

  Line 81: But simply seeing the tcpdump output on your laptop's terminal doesn't offer much difference to the local capture.

  Line 83: The true power the remote capture has is in being able to use the Wireshark installed on your machine to display the captured traffic. To do that we need to pipe the output of the `tcpdump` command to the `wireshark` command. This is done by adding the `-w -` option to the `tcpdump` command which tells it to write the captured traffic to the standard output. The output is then piped to the `wireshark` command which is invoked with the `-k -i -` options. The `-k` option tells wireshark to start capturing immediately and the `-i -` option tells it to read the input from the standard input.

  Line 91: This will start the capture from a given interface and redirect the received flow to the Wireshark!

Key observation: there is no `capture` command in `cmd/` (grep for "capture" found no command registration). The robot test `02-release-check.robot` runs `capture -t ${topo} --list` which would fail with "unknown command" — but wait, that's the intent: the test expects a nonzero rc and a specific error message "no spec.runState". An unknown command would produce rc != 0, but the error message wouldn't contain "no spec.runState", so `Should Contain ${message} no spec.runState` would fail. So the test is broken unless `capture` exists.

66: type Runtime struct {
67: 	client     dynamic.Interface
68: 	kubeClient kubernetes.Interface
69: 	restConfig *rest.Config
70: 	namespace  string
71: 	// labNamespaceOverride is set by --namespace or CLAB_KUBE_NAMESPACE. When
72: 	// empty, lab-scoped operations derive their namespace from the lab name.
73: 	labNamespaceOverride string
74: 	timeout              time.Duration
75: 	// kindLinkApplyMode resolves the default link apply mode a node kind declares.
76: 	// The plan uses it to predict the pod lifecycle impact of link changes.
77: 	kindLinkApplyMode func(kind string) string
78: 	// clients loads the Kubernetes clients on first use. Commands that only compile the
79: 	// topology (validate, deploy --emit-crs) never call it, so they work without a
80: 	// kubeconfig that loads. It is nil when the clients were injected (tests).
81: 	clients *clientLoader
82: 	// connected marks a runtime view whose client fields are populated.
83: 	connected bool
84: 	// identity is the configured identity of calls without one; in a connected view it is the
85: 	// identity the clients impersonate.
86: 	identity clablabruntime.Identity
87: 	// pollInterval overrides how often waits poll the cluster (tests).
88: 	pollInterval time.Duration
89: 	// support checks once per runtime instance, before the first cluster call, that the
90: 	// cluster runs a clabernetes release with the contract this runtime needs. Every view
91: 	// shares it. It is nil when the clients were injected (tests).
92: 	support *supportCheck
93: }
94: 
95: // kubeClients is the set of Kubernetes clients a runtime view operates with.
96: type kubeClients struct {
97: 	dynamic    dynamic.Interface
98: 	kube       kubernetes.Interface
99: 	restConfig *rest.Config
100: }
101: 
102: // clientLoader loads the kubeconfig once and builds, and caches, the Kubernetes clients of
103: // every identity from it.
104: type clientLoader struct {
105: 	loadConfig func() (*rest.Config, string, error)
106: 	newClients func(*rest.Config) (*kubeClients, error)
107: 
108: 	once      sync.Once
109: 	base      *rest.Config
110: 	namespace string
111: 	err       error
112: 
113: 	mu         sync.Mutex
114: 	byIdentity map[string]*kubeClients
115: }
116: 
117: func newClientLoader() *clientLoader {
118: 	return &clientLoader{
119: 		loadConfig: kubeClientConfig,
120: 		newClients: newKubeClients,
121: 	}
122: }
123: 
124: func newKubeClients(restConfig *rest.Config) (*kubeClients, error) {
125: 	client, err := dynamic.NewForConfig(restConfig)
126: 	if err != nil {
127: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes dynamic client: %w", err)
128: 	}
129: 
130: 	kubeClient, err := kubernetes.NewForConfig(restConfig)
131: 	if err != nil {
132: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes client: %w", err)
133: 	}
134: 
135: 	return &kubeClients{dynamic: client, kube: kubeClient, restConfig: restConfig}, nil
136: }
137: 
138: // load returns the clients of an identity. The impersonation is part of the rest config, so it
139: // applies to every transport built from it: REST calls, watches, log streams, and the SPDY and
140: // websocket upgrades of exec, attach and port-forward.
141: func (l *clientLoader) load(
142: 	identity clablabruntime.Identity,
143: ) (*kubeClients, string, error) {
144: 	l.once.Do(func() {
145: 		l.base, l.namespace, l.err = l.loadConfig()
146: 		if l.namespace == "" {
147: 			l.namespace = defaultNamespace
148: 		}
149: 	})
150: 	if l.err != nil {
151: 		return nil, "", l.err
152: 	}
153: 
154: 	key := identityKey(identity)
155: 
156: 	l.mu.Lock()
157: 	defer l.mu.Unlock()
158: 
159: 	if clients, ok := l.byIdentity[key]; ok {
160: 		return clients, l.namespace, nil
161: 	}
162: 
163: 	restConfig := rest.CopyConfig(l.base)
164: 	if !identity.IsZero() {
165: 		restConfig.Impersonate = rest.ImpersonationConfig{
166: 			UserName: identity.User,
167: 			Groups:   slices.Clone(identity.Groups),
168: 		}
169: 	}
170: 
171: 	clients, err := l.newClients(restConfig)
172: 	if err != nil {
173: 		return nil, "", err
174: 	}
175: 	if l.byIdentity == nil {
176: 		l.byIdentity = map[string]*kubeClients{}
177: 	}
178: 	l.byIdentity[key] = clients
179: 
180: 	return clients, l.namespace, nil
181: }
182: 
183: func identityKey(identity clablabruntime.Identity) string {
184: 	return identity.User + "\x00" + strings.Join(identity.Groups, "\x00")
185: }
186: 
187: // connect returns a view of the runtime with the Kubernetes clients of an identity populated,
188: // loading the kubeconfig on first use. A zero identity uses the runtime's configured identity.
189: // Every operation that reads or changes cluster state calls it first, so it also runs the
190: // clabernetes version check once per runtime instance, before the first cluster call.
191: func (r *Runtime) connect(
192: 	ctx context.Context,
193: 	identity clablabruntime.Identity,
194: ) (*Runtime, error) {
195: 	if identity.IsZero() {
196: 		identity = r.identity
197: 	}
198: 	if r.connected && identity.Equal(r.identity) {
199: 		return r, nil
200: 	}
201: 	if r.clients == nil {
202: 		// clients were injected (tests); they act as the identity they were built with
203: 		if err := r.support.ensure(ctx, r); err != nil {
204: 			return nil, err
205: 		}
206: 
207: 		return r, nil
208: 	}
209: 
210: 	clients, namespace, err := r.clients.load(identity)
211: 	if err != nil {
212: 		return nil, err
213: 	}
214: 
215: 	view := *r
216: 	view.client = clients.dynamic
217: 	view.kubeClient = clients.kube
218: 	view.restConfig = clients.restConfig
219: 	if view.namespace == "" {
220: 		view.namespace = namespace
221: 	}
222: 	view.identity = identity
223: 	view.connected = true
224: 
225: 	if err := r.support.ensure(ctx, &view); err != nil {
226: 		return nil, err
227: 	}
228: 
229: 	return &view, nil
230: }
231: 
232: func withKubernetesClientDebugLogs(ctx context.Context) context.Context {
233: 	verbosity := -1
234: 	if log.GetLevel() <= log.DebugLevel {
235: 		verbosity = 3
236: 	}
237: 	logger := funcr.New(func(prefix, args string) {
238: 		log.Debug("Kubernetes client", "log", strings.TrimSpace(prefix+" "+args))
239: 	}, funcr.Options{Verbosity: verbosity})
240: 
241: 	return klog.NewContext(ctx, logger)
242: }
243: 
244: func init() {
245: 	clablabruntime.Register(clablabruntime.ClabernetesRuntimeName, New)
246: }
247: 
248: // New returns the c9s lab runtime. It does not load the kubeconfig: the Kubernetes clients
249: // are created on the first operation that needs the cluster.
250: func New(cfg clablabruntime.Config) (clablabruntime.LabRuntime, error) {
251: 	return &Runtime{
252: 		labNamespaceOverride: configuredLabNamespace(cfg.Namespace),
253: 		timeout:              cfg.Timeout,
254: 		kindLinkApplyMode:    cfg.KindLinkApplyMode,
255: 		identity:             cfg.Identity,
256: 		clients:              newClientLoader(),
257: 		support:              &supportCheck{},
258: 	}, nil
259: }

267: 		return targets, namespace, known, nil
268: 	}
269: 
270: 	for _, nodeName := range req.Nodes {
271: 		resolved, ok := resolveKnownNodeName(known, nodeName)
272: 		if !ok {
273: 			return nil, "", nil, fmt.Errorf("node %q was not found in topology %s/%s",
274: 				nodeName, namespace, req.Name)
275: 		}
276: 		targets = append(targets, resolved)
277: 	}
278: 
279: 	return targets, namespace, known, nil
280: }

282: func (r *Runtime) patchNode(
283: 	ctx context.Context,
284: 	namespace,

286: 	patch map[string]any,
287: ) (*unstructured.Unstructured, error) {
288: 	data, err := json.Marshal(patch)
289: 	if err != nil {
290: 		return nil, err
291: 	}
292: 
293: 	return r.client.Resource(nodeGVR).Namespace(namespace).
294: 		Patch(ctx, name, types.MergePatchType, data, metav1.PatchOptions{})
295: }

297: // waitNodes polls the Nodes until done reports every one of them finished, within the request
298: // timeout. A timeout names each unfinished node with its observed state.
299: func (r *Runtime) waitNodes(
300: 	ctx context.Context,
301: 	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
302: 	namespace string,
303: 	nodes []*unstructured.Unstructured,
304: 	operation string,
305: 	done func(node *unstructured.Unstructured, stoppedPeers func() []string) (bool, string),
306: ) error {
307: 	waitCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, r.timeoutFor(req.Timeout))
308: 	defer cancel()
309: 
310: 	pending := make(map[string]string, len(nodes))
311: 	for _, node := range nodes {
312: 		pending[node.GetName()] = "not observed yet"
313: 	}
314: 
315: 	err := wait.PollUntilContextCancel(waitCtx, r.nodePollInterval(), true,
316: 		func(ctx context.Context) (bool, error) {
317: 			// the lab's run states are read at most once per poll, and only for a node that is
318: 			// up but not ready
319: 			var states *labRunStates
320: 			for name := range pending {
321: 				node, err := r.client.Resource(nodeGVR).Namespace(namespace).
322: 					Get(ctx, name, metav1.GetOptions{})
323: 				if err != nil {
324: 					return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to get c9s node %s/%s/%s: %w",
325: 						namespace, req.Name, name, err)
326: 				}
327: 				stoppedPeers := func() []string {
328: 					if states == nil {
329: 						loaded, err := r.labRunStates(ctx, req.Name, namespace)
330: 						if err != nil {
331: 							return nil
332: 						}
333: 						states = loaded
334: 					}
335: 
336: 					return states.stoppedPeers[name]
337: 				}
338: 				finished, state := done(node, stoppedPeers)
339: 				if finished {
340: 					delete(pending, name)
341: 					continue
342: 				}
343: 				pending[name] = state
344: 			}
345: 
346: 			return len(pending) == 0, nil
347: 		})
348: 	if err == nil {
349: 		return nil
350: 	}
351: 	if !errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) && !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
352: 		return err
353: 	}
354: 
355: 	names := make([]string, 0, len(pending))
356: 	for name := range pending {
357: 		names = append(names, name)
358: 	}
359: 	sort.Strings(names)
360: 
361: 	details := make([]string, 0, len(names))
362: 	for _, name := range names {
363: 		details = append(details, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s", name, pending[name]))
364: 	}
365: 
366: 	return fmt.Errorf("timed out waiting for the %s of c9s nodes in lab %s/%s (%s): %w",
367: 		operation, namespace, req.Name, strings.Join(details, "; "), err)
368: }

383: func nodeRunState(node *unstructured.Unstructured) string {
384: 	runState, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(node.Object, "spec", "runState")
385: 	if runState == "" {
386: 		return nodeRunStateRunning
387: 	}
388: 
389: 	return runState
390: }

392: func nodeReadiness(node *unstructured.Unstructured) string {
393: 	readiness, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(node.Object, "status", "readiness")
394: 
395: 	return readiness
396: }

398: type nodeStatusCondition struct {
399: 	status             string
400: 	reason             string
401: 	message            string
402: 	observedGeneration int64
403: }
404: 
405: func nodeCondition(node *unstructured.Unstructured, conditionType string) *nodeStatusCondition {
406: 	conditions, _, _ := unstructured.NestedSlice(node.Object, "status", "conditions")
407: 	for _, raw := range conditions {
408: 		condition, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
409: 		if !ok || condition["type"] != conditionType {
410: 			continue
411: 		}
412: 
413: 		result := &nodeStatusCondition{
414: 			status:             fmt.Sprint(condition["status"]),
415: 			observedGeneration: int64(intField(condition["observedGeneration"])),
416: 		}
417: 		result.reason, _ = condition["reason"].(string)
418: 		result.message, _ = condition["message"].(string)
419: 
420: 		return result
421: 	}
422: 
423: 	return nil
424: }

426: // labRunStates is the run state view of a lab: its Nodes and, per node, the link peers whose
427: // pod is stopped. clabernetes keeps a node's connectivity not ready while a link peer is
428: // stopped (its wire has no far end), so waits accept a node whose containers are ready and
429: // whose only missing peers are stopped ones.
430: type labRunStates struct {
431: 	nodes        map[string]*unstructured.Unstructured
432: 	networkModes map[string]string
433: 	stoppedPeers map[string][]string
434: }
435: 
436: func (r *Runtime) labRunStates(
437: 	ctx context.Context,
438: 	lab,
439: 	namespace string,
440: ) (*labRunStates, error) {
441: 	nodeList, err := r.nodesForTopology(ctx, lab, namespace)
442: 	if err != nil {
443: 		return nil, err
444: 	}
445: 	links, err := r.primitiveResourcesForTopology(ctx, linkGVR, lab, namespace)
446: 	if err != nil {
447: 		return nil, err
448: 	}
449: 
450: 	states := &labRunStates{
451: 		nodes:        make(map[string]*unstructured.Unstructured, len(nodeList.Items)),
452: 		networkModes: make(map[string]string, len(nodeList.Items)),
453: 		stoppedPeers: map[string][]string{},
454: 	}
455: 	for idx := range nodeList.Items {
456: 		node := &nodeList.Items[idx]
457: 		states.nodes[node.GetName()] = node
458: 		states.networkModes[node.GetName()] = nodeNetworkMode(node)
459: 	}
460: 
461: 	for idx := range links.Items {
462: 		a, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(
463: 			links.Items[idx].Object,
464: 			"spec",
465: 			"endpointA",
466: 			"nodeName",
467: 		)
468: 		b, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(
469: 			links.Items[idx].Object,
470: 			"spec",
471: 			"endpointB",
472: 			"nodeName",
473: 		)
474: 		if states.stopped(b) {
475: 			states.stoppedPeers[a] = append(states.stoppedPeers[a], b)
476: 		}
477: 		if states.stopped(a) {
478: 			states.stoppedPeers[b] = append(states.stoppedPeers[b], a)
479: 		}
480: 	}
481: 
482: 	return states, nil
483: }
484: 
485: // stopped reports whether a node's pod is stopped or stopping: the run state of the node's
486: // primary governs the pod it runs in.
487: func (s *labRunStates) stopped(nodeName string) bool {
488: 	primary := s.nodes[resolvePrimaryNode(nodeName, s.networkModes)]
489: 
490: 	return primary != nil && nodeRunState(primary) == nodeRunStateStopped
491: }
492: 
493: // waitsOnlyForStoppedPeers reports whether a running node that is not ready has ready containers
494: // and at least one stopped link peer, the state clabernetes reports for such a node.
495: func waitsOnlyForStoppedPeers(node *unstructured.Unstructured, stoppedPeers []string) bool {
496: 	if len(stoppedPeers) == 0 || nodeRunState(node) == nodeRunStateStopped {
497: 		return false
498: 	}
499: 	containers := nodeCondition(node, nodeConditionContainersReady)
500: 
501: 	return containers != nil && containers.status == string(metav1.ConditionTrue)
502: }
503: 
504: // settledNode reports whether a deploy or start no longer waits for a node: it is ready, it is
505: // stopped on purpose, or it is up and only waits for stopped link peers. The reason describes a
506: // settled node that is not ready.
507: func (s *labRunStates) settledNode(name string) (bool, string) {
508: 	node := s.nodes[name]
509: 	if node == nil {
510: 		return false, ""
511: 	}
512: 	if s.stopped(name) {
513: 		return true, "stopped"
514: 	}
515: 	if nodeReadiness(node) == nodeReadinessReady {
516: 		return true, ""
517: 	}
518: 	if peers := s.stoppedPeers[name]; waitsOnlyForStoppedPeers(node, peers) {
519: 		sorted := append([]string(nil), peers...)
520: 		sort.Strings(sorted)
521: 
522: 		return true, "link peers stopped: " + strings.Join(sorted, ", ")
523: 	}
524: 
525: 	return false, ""
526: }

Cobra with unknown command prints "Error: unknown command "capture" for "containerlab"" to stderr and exits with code 1 (with SilenceUsage set, unknown command still prints usage? Actually for unknown subcommands, cobra returns error from Execute → prints "Error: unknown command..." and usage unless silenced). The message won't contain "no spec.runState" → `Should Contain` fails → test fails. So the added suite is broken when CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG is set. Wait — actually, could `capture` be provided by the clabwire companion (the "clabwire capture contract")? The comment says "the clabwire capture contract (--nodeName, repeated --interface, --format pcapng, --list-interfaces)". This suggests a `containerlab capture` command implemented by clabwire integration — perhaps in a companion PR not part of this diff. Regardless, in this tree the command doesn't exist, so the test fails. This is a legitimate P3 finding anchored to the new test file.

Hmm, but also — even if `capture` existed, would it produce "no spec.runState"? Yes, via connect.

Now let me finish the diff reading (offset 3562 to 3774), which covers the remaining robot test diff. Then examine remaining pieces:

- `reconcile.go` carryOverNodeRunState (already largely understood).
- Check `01-linux-lifecycle.robot` changes around node run-state waiting.

Also one more potential issue in `support.go` `ensure`: the mutex is held during the OpenAPI fetch — network call under lock. Concurrent callers block on the first check; that's intended (once-per-instance). Fine.

One more thing in `ensure`: `apierrors.IsNotFound(err)` — `Do(ctx).Raw()` returns errors; for 404, Raw() returns an error created from the response; IsNotFound works on StatusError. Discovery REST client's Raw returns apierrors? It returns error from transformUnstructuredResponseError — it creates StatusError for 404? Actually `Do(ctx).Raw()` — for non-2xx, Result.Raw returns an error; if the response body is a Status JSON, it converts to StatusError. If the API isn't served at all, the path returns 404 with a Status body ("the server could not find the requested resource"). apierrors.IsNotFound checks for StatusError with reason NotFound — plausible. But if the body isn't a Status object, `Raw()` may return a generic error → treated as transient error → retried each call (never cached). Acceptable.

Now, potential real correctness issue: `checkNodeRunStateSchema` iterates `doc.Components.Schemas` — but Kubernetes OpenAPI v3 documents for CRDs use `"x-kubernetes-group-version-kind"` — fine.

Another consideration: `resolveOpenAPIProperty`'s AllOf handling: `case len(schema.AllOf) == 1` — if schema has AllOf with more than 1 entry, returns false. OK for CRD schemas.

3702: --- /dev/null
3703: +++ b/tests/14-clabernetes/02-release-check.robot
3704: @@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
3705: +*** Comments ***
3706: +The c9s runtime refuses clusters whose clabernetes release lacks Node run state and the clabwire
3707: +capture contract. This suite needs a second cluster that serves the older c9s.run CRDs (for
3708: +example a KinD cluster with only the clabernetes 0.10.1 CRDs applied); set
3709: +CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG to its kubeconfig. Without it, the suite is skipped.
3710: +
3711: +
3712: +*** Settings ***
3713: +Library             OperatingSystem
3714: +Library             Process
3715: +Resource            ../common.robot
3716: +
3717: +Suite Setup         Setup
3718: +Test Tags           clabernetes    c9s
3719: +
3720: +
3721: +*** Variables ***
3722: +${runtime}          c9s
3723: +${topo}             ${CURDIR}/01-linux-lifecycle.clab.yml
3724: +${lab-namespace}    c9s-c9s-linux-lifecycle
3725: +${required}         clabernetes with Node run state and the clabwire capture contract (0.11 or newer)
3726: +
3727: +
3728: +*** Test Cases ***
3729: +Cluster commands fail before the first cluster call
3730: +    FOR    ${args}    IN
3731: +    ...    inspect --all
3732: +    ...    deploy -t ${topo}
3733: +    ...    stop -t ${topo} -n server
3734: +    ...    capture -t ${topo} --list
3735: +    ...    events --format json
3736: +        ${output} =    Run Old Cluster Command    ${args}
3737: +        Should Not Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
3738: +        # the error box wraps long lines
3739: +        ${message} =    Evaluate    " ".join($output.stderr.split())
3740: +        Should Contain    ${message}    no spec.runState
3741: +        Should Contain    ${message}    ${required}
3742: +    END
3743: +
3744: +    ${namespace} =    Process.Run Process
3745: +    ...    kubectl --kubeconfig %{CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG} get namespace ${lab-namespace} --ignore-not-found -o name
3746: +    ...    shell=True
3747: +    Should Be Empty    ${namespace.stdout}
3748: +
3749: +Offline commands skip the check
3750: +    ${validate} =    Run Old Cluster Command    validate -t ${topo}
3751: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${validate.rc}    0
3752: +
3753: +    ${emit} =    Run Old Cluster Command    deploy -t ${topo} --emit-crs
3754: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${emit.rc}    0
3755: +    Should Contain    ${emit.stdout}    kind: Topology
3756: +
3757: +
3758: +*** Keywords ***
3759: +Setup
3760: +    Skip If    '${runtime}' != 'c9s'    This suite targets the c9s runtime.
3761: +    ${old} =    Get Environment Variable    CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG    ${EMPTY}
3762: +    Skip If    '${old}' == ''    CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG is not set
3763: +
3764: +Run Old Cluster Command
3765: +    [Arguments]    ${args}
3766: +    ${output} =    Process.Run Process
3767: +    ...    ${CLAB_BIN} --runtime ${runtime} ${args}
3768: +    ...    shell=True
3769: +    ...    timeout=60s
3770: +    ...    env:KUBECONFIG=%{CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG}
3771: +    ...    env:CLAB_KUBECONFIG=%{CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG}
3772: +    Log    stdout:${\n}${output.stdout}    console=${True}
3773: +    Log    stderr:${\n}${output.stderr}    console=${True}
3774: +    RETURN    ${output}

(End of file - total 3774 lines)

Now check `nodeConditionCurrent`: `condition == nil || condition.observedGeneration >= generation`. OK.

Potential issue: `newRestartToken` uses wall-clock; two restarts within the same nanosecond unlikely. Fine.

Kubernetes CRD\n// defaulting materializes fields such as false booleans and zero-second probe configuration in\n// stored objects even when the renderer omitted them. Those values are declaratively equivalent;\n// treating them as drift would make every plan and reconciliation report an update forever.\nfunc normalizeAPIDefaultedJSON(value any) any {\n\tswitch typed := value.(type) {\n\tcase map[string]any:\n\t\tresult := make(map[string]any, len(typed))\n\t\tfor key, child := range typed {\n\t\t\tnormalized := normalizeAPIDefaultedJSON(child)\n\t\t\tif !isZeroJSONValue(normalized) {\n\t\t\t\tresult[key] = normalized\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\t\treturn result\n\tcase []any:\n\t\tresult := make([]any, len(typed))\n\t\tfor idx := range typed {\n\t\t\tresult[idx] = normalizeAPIDefaultedJSON(typed[idx])\n\t\t}\n\n\t\treturn result\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn normalizeJSONNumber(value)\n\t}\n}\n\n// normalizeJSONNumber gives every number one Go type. 3. Check `01-linux-lifecycle.robot`'s new test "Apply while server is stopped" — expects stderr contains "C9s lab is ready apart from stopped nodes" and "server (stopped)". In lifecycle.go: log.Info("C9s lab is ready apart from stopped nodes", ..., "nodes", strings.Join(notes, ", ")) — notes format "server (stopped)" from settledNode returning "stopped" reason → note = "server (stopped)" ✓.

100: ///
101: 
102: The c9s runtime currently supports the main lab lifecycle and node operations:
103: 
104: | Command | c9s behavior |
105: | ------- | ------------ |
106: | `deploy` | creates the `Topology` resource and waits for readiness; `--no-topology-cr` creates `NodeProfile`, `Link`, and `Node` resources directly instead |
107: | `destroy` | deletes the lab's resources and its containerlab-managed namespace |
108: | `inspect` | reads Node, Pod, and service status |
109: | `exec` | execs directly into the node's device container |
110: | `start` | sets the node's `spec.runState` to `Running` |
111: | `stop` | sets the node's `spec.runState` to `Stopped` |
112: | `restart` | requests a Pod replacement with a `c9s.run/restart-requested` token |
113: | `save` | runs the node's save lifecycle inside its device container |
114: | `events` | watches Clabernetes resources and pods |
115: | `validate` | checks c9s compatibility without creating Kubernetes resources |
116: | `deploy --dry-run` | compiles and diffs Namespace, ConfigMap, NodeProfile, Link, and Node resources without changing them |
117: | `deploy --emit-crs` | prints the Namespace, ConfigMap, and Topology (or NodeProfile, Link, and Node) manifests deploy would create, without contacting the cluster |
118: 
119: ## Requirements
120: 
121: The c9s runtime expects:
122: 
123: - a reachable kubernetes cluster
124: - kubernetes 1.31 or newer
125: - clabernetes with Node run state and the clabwire capture contract (0.11 or
126:   newer) installed in the cluster
127: - the Clabernetes manager running and watching all lab namespaces
128: - kubernetes RBAC allowing containerlab to manage the required resources
129: - permission for lab namespaces to run the privileged c9s connectivity
130:   init-sidecar
131: 
132: /// note
133: Containerlab creates a dedicated namespace for each c9s lab. The kube identity
134: therefore needs cluster-scoped permission to get, create, and delete namespaces
135: unless you select an existing namespace with `CLAB_KUBE_NAMESPACE`.
136: ///
137: 
138: ### Required clabernetes release
139: 
140: Containerlab needs a clabernetes release that has:
141: 
142: - Node run state: `nodes.c9s.run` `spec.runState` (`Running` | `Stopped`), the
143:   `Stopped` condition, and restart requests through the
144:   `c9s.run/restart-requested` annotation
145: - the clabwire packet capture contract: `--nodeName`, repeated `--interface`,
146:   `--format pcapng` and `--list-interfaces`
147: - the namespace-bindable `clabernetes-lab-viewer` and `clabernetes-lab-editor`
148:   roles
149: 
150: Both features ship in the same release, so containerlab checks one field: the
151: published OpenAPI schema of `nodes.c9s.run` (`/openapi/v3/apis/c9s.run/v1alpha1`)
152: must have `spec.runState`. Every authenticated user may read that document, so
153: the check needs no extra RBAC. It runs once per command (once per runtime
154: instance for library users) before the first cluster call. Commands that do not
155: contact the cluster (`validate`, `deploy --emit-crs`, `graph`) skip it. Against
156: an older release every other command fails like this:
157: 
158: ```text
159: the clabernetes release on this cluster is not supported: nodes.c9s.run has no
160: spec.runState (Node run state); the c9s runtime needs clabernetes with Node run
161: state and the clabwire capture contract (0.11 or newer)
162: ```
163: 
164: Library users can run the check up front with
165: `(*core.CLab).CheckLabRuntimeSupport(ctx)` or the optional
166: `labruntime.SupportChecker` interface; the error wraps
167: `labruntime.ErrUnsupportedRuntimeVersion`.
168: 
169: See the
170: [c9s cluster requirements](https://c9s.run/docs/installation#cluster-requirements)
171: for Pod Security Admission, worker kernel, network policy, registry, and KVM
172: requirements.
173: 
174: ## Selecting the cluster
175: 
176: The runtime uses the kubernetes client-go configuration loader. It selects the
177: kubeconfig in this order:
178: 
179: 1. `CLAB_KUBECONFIG`, when set
180: 2. normal client-go kubeconfig loading rules
181: 
182: You can override the kube context with:
183: 
184: ```bash
185: export CLAB_KUBE_CONTEXT=<context-name>
186: ```
187: 
188: To deploy into an existing namespace instead of a per-lab namespace, use the
189: global `--namespace` option:

(Showing lines 100-189 of 1183. Use offset=190 to continue.)

        "text": "///\n\nThe c9s runtime currently supports the main lab lifecycle and node operations:\n\n| Command | c9s behavior |\n| ------- | ------------ |\n| `deploy` | creates the `Topology` resource and waits for readiness; `--no-topology-cr` creates `NodeProfile`, `Link`, and `Node` resources directly instead |\n| `destroy` | deletes the lab's resources and its containerlab-managed namespace |\n| `inspect` | reads Node, Pod, and service status |\n| `exec` | execs directly into the node's device container |\n| `start` | sets the node's `spec.runState` to `Running` |\n| `stop` | sets the node's `spec.runState` to `Stopped` |\n| `restart` | requests a Pod replacement with a `c9s.run/restart-requested` token |\n| `save` | runs the node's save lifecycle inside its device container |\n| `events` | watches Clabernetes resources and pods |\n| `validate` | checks c9s compatibility without creating Kubernetes resources |\n| `deploy --dry-run` | compiles and diffs Namespace, ConfigMap, NodeProfile, Link, and Node resources without changing them |\n| `deploy --emit-crs` | prints the Namespace, ConfigMap, and Topology (or NodeProfile, Link, and Node) manifests deploy would create, without contacting the cluster |\n\n## Requirements\n\nThe c9s runtime expects:\n\n- a reachable kubernetes cluster\n- kubernetes 1.31 or newer\n- clabernetes with Node run state and the clabwire capture contract (0.11 or\n  newer) installed in the cluster\n- the Clabernetes manager running and watching all lab namespaces\n- kubernetes RBAC allowing containerlab to manage the required resources\n- permission for lab namespaces to run the privileged c9s connectivity\n  init-sidecar\n\n/// note\nContainerlab creates a dedicated namespace for each c9s lab. The kube identity\ntherefore needs cluster-scoped permission to get, create, and delete namespaces\nunless you select an existing namespace with `CLAB_KUBE_NAMESPACE`.\n///\n\n### Required clabernetes release\n\nContainerlab needs a clabernetes release that has:\n\n- Node run state: `nodes.c9s.run` `spec.runState` (`Running` | `Stopped`), the\n  `Stopped` condition, and restart requests through the\n  `c9s.run/restart-requested` annotation\n- the clabwire packet capture contract: `--nodeName`, repeated `--interface`,\n  `--format pcapng` and `--list-interfaces`\n- the namespace-bindable `clabernetes-lab-viewer` and `clabernetes-lab-editor`\n  roles\n\nBoth features ship in the same release, so containerlab checks one field: the\npublished OpenAPI schema of `nodes.c9s.run` (`/openapi/v3/apis/c9s.run/v1alpha1`)\nmust have `spec.runState`. Every authenticated user may read that document, so\nthe check needs no extra RBAC. It runs once per command (once per runtime\ninstance for library users) before the first cluster call. Commands that do not\ncontact the cluster (`validate`, `deploy --emit-crs`, `graph`) skip it. Against\nan older release every other command fails like this:\n\n```text\nthe clabernetes release on this cluster is not supported: nodes.c9s.run has no\nspec.runState (Node run state); the c9s runtime needs clabernetes with Node run\nstate and the clabwire capture contract (0.11 or newer)\n```\n\nLibrary users can run the check up front with\n`(*core.CLab).CheckLabRuntimeSupport(ctx)` or the optional\n`labruntime.SupportChecker` interface; the error wraps\n`labruntime.ErrUnsupportedRuntimeVersion`.\n\nSee the\n[c9s cluster requirements](https://c9s.run/docs/installation#cluster-requirements)\nfor Pod Security Admission, worker kernel, network policy, registry, and KVM\nrequirements.\n\n## Selecting the cluster\n\nThe runtime uses the kubernetes client-go configuration loader. It selects the\nkubeconfig in this order:\n\n1. `CLAB_KUBECONFIG`, when set\n2. normal client-go kubeconfig loading rules\n\nYou can override the kube context with:\n\n```bash\nexport CLAB_KUBE_CONTEXT=<context-name>\n```\n\nTo deploy into an existing namespace instead of a per-lab namespace, use the\nglobal `--namespace` option:",

        "truncated": true
      }
