# PR Review: clabernetes release gating (Node run state support check)

## Summary

The PR adds a release gate for the clabernetes runtime: a once-per-runtime-instance check that fetches the cluster's OpenAPI v3 schema at `/openapi/v3/apis/c9s.run/v1alpha1` and verifies `nodes.c9s.run` has `spec.runState`, failing with a wrapped `labruntime.ErrUnsupportedRuntimeVersion` otherwise. It also adds Node run-state machinery (`stop`/`start`/`restart` via `spec.runState` and a `c9s.run/restart-requested` annotation), run-state carry-over on reconcile, "lab settles with stopped nodes" waiting semantics, a new `(*core.CLab).CheckLabRuntimeSupport` API, and Go/robot test coverage.

The implementation is clean and well-factored: the support check is correctly cached (unsupported results and success are memoized, transient errors retry), views run the check under the caller's identity, offline commands (`validate`, `deploy --emit-crs`, `graph`) skip it, and the reconcile carry-over correctly treats `spec.runState` as operational state. The docs match the implementation, including the exact error text. One real defect: the new release-check robot suite invokes a `capture` command that is not registered anywhere in this tree, so the suite fails at that item whenever it is actually exercised.

## Severity Summary

| Priority | Count | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P0 | 0 | — |
| P1 | 0 | — |
| P2 | 0 | — |
| P3 | 1 | Robot release-check suite runs a nonexistent `capture` command |
| P4 | 0 | — |

## Findings

### P3 — Robot release-check suite runs a nonexistent `capture` command

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Location:** [`tests/14-clabernetes/02-release-check.robot#L26-L38`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/tests/14-clabernetes/02-release-check.robot#L26-L38)

**Problem:** The new FOR loop in the "Cluster commands fail before the first cluster call" test runs `capture -t ${topo} --list` and asserts that the command's stderr contains `no spec.runState` and the required-release string. No `capture` subcommand exists in this tree: `subcommandRegisterFuncs()` in [`cmd/root.go#L25-L45`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/cmd/root.go#L25-L45) registers 17 commands (`version`, `completion`, `deploy`, `destroy`, `start`, `stop`, `restart`, `exec`, `generate`, `graph`, `events`, `inspect`, `logs`, `redeploy`, `save`, `tools`, `validate`) and none of the `Use:` literals anywhere in `cmd/` is `capture` (the capture contract is only mentioned in docs and error strings).

**Trigger:** Running the suite with `CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG` set (the suite skips otherwise, per its Setup keyword).

**Impact:** Cobra rejects the unknown command with `unknown command "capture" for "containerlab"` and non-zero rc, so the `Should Contain ${message} no spec.runState` assertion fails regardless of the old cluster's state. The release-gating suite — the exact scenario this PR's support check is built for — cannot pass, and the follow-up assertions verifying that `deploy` created no namespace (lines 40–43) are never reached for that item. This likely depends on a companion "clabwire capture" PR; merged in isolation the PR fails its own test suite.

**Suggestion:** Either ship the `capture` command in this PR, drop the `capture` item from the FOR loop with a comment noting the dependency, or skip that individual item when the binary under test lacks the command so the remaining release-gate assertions still run.
</details>

## Coverage Notes

- Source-only review of a read-only snapshot; no tests, formatters, or linters were executed. The Go and robot test suites were reviewed statically.
- All 25 paths from `manifest.json` were examined via `diff.txt` plus targeted reads of the head files (the diff tail beyond line ~3861 was covered by reading the head files directly, including both robot suites, the docs section, `reconcile.go`, `labruntime_access.go`, and `cmd/root.go`).
- Resolved candidate findings that turned out fine: `${lab-namespace}` in `02-release-check.robot` is a deliberate literal (`c9s-c9s-linux-lifecycle`), matching `01-linux-lifecycle.robot`; `stop -n` shorthand for `--node` exists in `cmd/stop.go`; `events --format json` is valid; `CLAB_KUBECONFIG` exists in `clabernetes.go` and the docs; the documented error text matches `support.go`; the `spec.labels` removal in `primitives.go` is intentional (labels are copied into Node metadata) with test coverage in `nodes_test.go`; the `connect` early-return cannot skip the support check, since views are copies whose ensure already ran at creation.
- The OpenAPI-based check itself (schema fetch, `#/components/schemas/` reference parsing, ensure caching, per-view identity) is covered by `TestCheckNodeRunStateSchema`, `TestSupportCheckRunsOnceBeforeTheFirstClusterCall`, `TestSupportCheckRetriesFailedRequestsAndRemembersSuccess`, and `TestSupportCheckReadsTheOpenAPIDocumentAsTheCaller`; the robot suite's behavior against a real 0.10.1 CRD cluster could only be verified by inspection since it needs an external cluster.

# PR Review: clabernetes release gating (Node run state support check)

## Summary

The PR adds a release gate for the clabernetes runtime: a once-per-runtime-instance check that fetches the cluster's OpenAPI v3 schema at `/openapi/v3/apis/c9s.run/v1alpha1` and verifies `nodes.c9s.run` has `spec.runState`, failing with a wrapped `labruntime.ErrUnsupportedRuntimeVersion` otherwise. It also adds Node run-state machinery (`stop`/`start`/`restart` via `spec.runState` and a `c9s.run/restart-requested` annotation), run-state carry-over on reconcile, "lab settles with stopped nodes" waiting semantics, a new `(*core.CLab).CheckLabRuntimeSupport` API, and Go/robot test coverage.

The implementation is clean and well-factored: the support check is correctly cached (unsupported results and success are memoized, transient errors retry), views run the check under the caller's identity, offline commands (`validate`, `deploy --emit-crs`, `graph`) skip it, and the reconcile carry-over correctly treats `spec.runState` as operational state. The docs match the implementation, including the exact error text. One real defect: the new release-check robot suite invokes a `capture` command that is not registered anywhere in this tree, so the suite fails at that item whenever it is actually exercised.

## Severity Summary

| Priority | Count | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P0 | 0 | — |
| P1 | 0 | — |
| P2 | 0 | — |
| P3 | 1 | Robot release-check suite runs a nonexistent `capture` command |
| P4 | 0 | — |

## Findings

### P3 — Robot release-check suite runs a nonexistent `capture` command

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Location:** [`tests/14-clabernetes/02-release-check.robot#L26-L38`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/tests/14-clabernetes/02-release-check.robot#L26-L38)

**Problem:** The FOR loop in the "Cluster commands fail before the first cluster call" test includes `capture -t ${topo} --list` (line 30) and asserts stderr contains `no spec.runState` and the required-release string. No `capture` subcommand exists in this tree: `subcommandRegisterFuncs()` in [`cmd/root.go#L25-L45`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ae844d3334bb3a7802f28d5aec90766028668a31/cmd/root.go#L25-L45) registers exactly 17 commands (`version`, `completion`, `deploy`, `destroy`, `start`, `stop`, `restart`, `exec`, `generate`, `graph`, `events`, `inspect`, `logs`, `redeploy`, `save`, `tools`, `validate`), and no `Use:` literal anywhere in `cmd/` is `capture` — the capture contract is only mentioned in docs and error strings.

**Trigger:** Running the suite with `CLAB_C9S_OLD_KUBECONFIG` set (the suite skips otherwise, per its Setup keyword).

**Impact:** Cobra rejects the unknown command with `unknown command "capture" for "containerlab"` and non-zero rc, so the `Should Contain ${message} no spec.runState` assertion fails regardless of the old cluster's state. The release-gating suite — the exact scenario this PR's support check is built for — cannot pass, and the follow-up assertion that `deploy` created no namespace (lines 40–43) is never reached. This likely depends on a companion "clabwire capture" PR; merged in isolation the PR fails its own test suite.

**Suggestion:** Either ship the `capture` command in this PR, drop the `capture` item from the FOR loop with a comment noting the dependency, or skip that individual item when the binary under test lacks the command so the remaining release-gate assertions still run.
</details>

## Coverage Notes

- Source-only review of a read-only snapshot; no tests, formatters, or linters were executed. The Go and robot test suites were reviewed statically.
- All 25 paths from `manifest.json` were examined via `diff.txt` plus targeted reads of the head files (the diff tail beyond line ~3861 was covered by reading the head files directly, including both robot suites, the docs section, `reconcile.go`, `labruntime_access.go`, and `cmd/root.go`).
- Resolved candidate findings that turned out fine: `${lab-namespace}` in `02-release-check.robot` is a deliberate literal (`c9s-c9s-linux-lifecycle`), matching `01-linux-lifecycle.robot`; `stop -n` shorthand for `--node` exists in `cmd/stop.go`; `events --format json` is valid; `CLAB_KUBECONFIG` exists in `clabernetes.go` and the docs; the documented error text matches `support.go`; the `spec.labels` removal in `primitives.go` is intentional (labels are copied into Node metadata) with test coverage in `nodes_test.go`; the `connect` early-return cannot skip the support check, since views are copies whose ensure already ran at creation.
- The OpenAPI-based check itself (schema fetch, `#/components/schemas/` reference parsing, ensure caching, per-view identity) is covered by `TestCheckNodeRunStateSchema`, `TestSupportCheckRunsOnceBeforeTheFirstClusterCall`, `TestSupportCheckRetriesFailedRequestsAndRemembersSuccess`, and `TestSupportCheckReadsTheOpenAPIDocumentAsTheCaller`; the robot suite's behavior against a real 0.10.1 CRD cluster could only be verified by inspection since it needs an external cluster.
